item.title: LocalePilot 1.0.0
item.description:
First public release of LocalePilot for macOS.

LocalePilot is a local-first workbench for developers who ship apps in several languages. It takes you from "new strings to translate" to "files ready to review in Git", with the AI model or translation service of your choice. Your files stay on your Mac: text only goes to an AI or translation provider you configured, when you translate, add a language with automatic translation, run an AI audit, adapt a store listing or test a connection. File names and paths are never sent.

What you can do

  • Install from the disk image: open the .dmg, drag LocalePilot into Applications and open it from there. If you start it from Downloads or the disk image, LocalePilot offers to install itself in Applications, so that updates keep working.
  • Open a project folder of localization files: nested and flat JSON, multi-language JSON (one file with a section per language) and Flutter ARB. Each detected language is shown with its name and code (and a flag when it has a region) before you open the project. Duplicate keys are refused at import, never silently overwritten. Files that iCloud Drive or another cloud service has not downloaded yet are listed as waiting, with a button to download them. If you move or rename a project folder, LocalePilot offers to follow it and keeps your drafts and settings.
  • Apple formats: .strings files in <locale>.lproj folders (UTF-8 or UTF-16, written back in their original encoding) and String Catalogs (.xcstrings), with plurals for every category the target language needs and device variations. Exported catalogs build in Xcode and stay unchanged when Xcode syncs them. When you add a language to .strings files, add the new .lproj folder to your Xcode project. .stringsdict is not supported, and catalog keys that use substitutions are kept as they are but not shown.
  • See every problem before you export: missing and empty values, keys present only in a translation, placeholder mismatches (ICU, {{name}}, tags, printf and Apple formats such as %@ and %1$@), invalid ICU messages (blocking, with a message that says what is wrong), ICU plural and select risks, plural forms the target language needs, source text copied into a translation, text that looks like the wrong language, Markdown or HTML drift, whitespace drift, unusual length and glossary violations. Some problems come with a one-click fix.
  • Review in a table: edit cells by hand, filter by status (to translate, AI drafts, needs review, approved), approve one cell or a selection, and edit ICU plurals and selects branch by branch. An inspector shows the key's context, its other languages and whether a value comes from a file, from the AI or from you. Right-to-left languages such as Arabic and Hebrew read correctly in the table, the editor and the preview.
  • Translate with AI on a selection or a filtered batch, with a local model (Ollama, LM Studio) or a cloud model with your own key (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek). A run stops at once with a clear message when a key is refused or the credit is exhausted, and waits when a provider asks to slow down. Each action tells you which cells and languages it will touch, and AI results stay drafts until you review them. A batch can be run again with another provider or model.
  • Audit existing translations with AI, from Translate, Review or the command palette: the model rereads translations against their source, context and glossary, reports problems and suggests corrections. A correction becomes an AI draft to review. On a value you reviewed, approved or edited by hand, it waits for your decision instead, and stays waiting after you close the dialog or the app.
  • Use a translation service for simple strings: DeepL, Microsoft Translator, Google Cloud Translation, or a local LibreTranslate server. Placeholders are protected, and ICU messages are refused rather than broken. Settings show when each provider's connection was last tested.
  • Keep your terminology: a project glossary with invariant terms, forbidden terms and optional per-language translations, shown for the target language in the context panel. It guides AI requests and QA flags translations that ignore it. With DeepL, LocalePilot keeps one glossary per language pair in your DeepL account, replaces it instead of piling up new ones, and tells you when the account has no room left.
  • Add a language from the source structure, and translate it right away if a provider is set up.
  • Prepare your store listings in the fastlane files you already publish: App Store (name, subtitle, promotional text, description, keywords, release notes) and Google Play (title, short and full description, changelogs). Store limits are checked as you type, the AI can adapt a listing to each market, a market can be linked to its counterpart on the other store, and each field can be approved. LocalePilot writes the files; it sends nothing to Apple or Google.
  • Export without breaking your files: you review every change first, the original structure and metadata are preserved where the format allows (ARB and .strings files only change on the lines you changed), changes made on disk since import are merged or shown as conflicts, a backup is made before anything is overwritten (the first version of each file is always kept), and an interrupted export can be resumed. When you come back to LocalePilot after editing a file in another app, it offers to reload it. Files with blocking problems can be left out while the others are written.
  • Work from the keyboard: command palette (⌘K), help from anywhere (?), ⌘↩ to save and go to the next entry, ⌘⇧↩ to approve and go to the next one, ⌘U for the next untranslated entry.
  • Light, dark or system theme, light by default.
  • Interface in English, French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese.
  • Report a problem if something goes wrong: LocalePilot keeps a local journal for two weeks and shows you the anonymized report, written in English, before you send it by email. Nothing leaves your Mac unless you send it.

Free and Pro

  • Free: 1 project, up to 300 source keys per project, local AI (Ollama, LM Studio) and LibreTranslate. A larger project opens read-only, so you can browse it and see its QA, and adding keys stops at the limit.
  • Pro: more than one project, projects of any size, cloud AI providers and translation services, AI audit, glossary and store listings.
  • 14-day Pro trial, with no payment asked. When it ends, LocalePilot goes back to the free version; your files and past exports stay untouched.
  • Pro licence: a one-time purchase that never expires, usable on up to 3 Macs. It includes every 1.x version, plus any major version released within 12 months of purchase. After that, you keep your version and can upgrade to the next major version at a reduced price. It is bought through Polar, which handles payment and invoices. LocalePilot keeps working offline for up to 30 days between licence checks, including when a check fails because of a network error. You manage the Macs that use your licence in the Polar customer portal.

Updates

LocalePilot checks for a new version once a day and installs it only when you click. The free version receives every update too. You can also choose Check for Updates… in the LocalePilot menu.

Good to know

  • Requires macOS 13 Ventura or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.
  • The app is signed with a Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple.
  • Licence checks and cloud providers use your Mac's proxy settings, including automatic proxy configuration.
  • LocalePilot runs in the macOS App Sandbox: it only reads and writes the folders you open.
  • It is comfortable with projects of a few thousand keys. Very large projects (around 10,000 keys in 20 languages) still work, with slower editing.
  • Windows and Linux builds are not part of this release.
